pilots.narrow_loop: Turn a thirty-day owner-absence answer into a first working dependency map.
pilots.larger_loop: Can clearing that map become a bounded fixed-fee service?

youtube.spoken_copy: Explain how your business runs for thirty days without using the word "I." "I call the customers. I approve the exceptions. I know where the records are." If the answer keeps falling back to the owner, circle it. Beside each circle, write who else could act, what they would need and what stops if the owner is not there. That is a first working map of where the business still depends on one person. That map does not prove the business would fail or sell for less. It shows what still lives in one person's head. EP007 asks whether clearing that working map can become a fixed-fee business.
youtube.standalone_payoff: The viewer can draft a working owner-dependency map from the thirty-day answer.
youtube.episode_extension: The bounded service, its exclusions and willingness-to-pay test.
youtube.cta: EP007 asks whether clearing that working map can become a fixed-fee business.
youtube.cliffhanger_line: Could clearing that map become a fixed-fee business?

linkedin.spoken_copy: A profitable P and L can still hide how much of the business lives in one person's head. Ask: "How would this business run for thirty days without the owner?" Then answer without using the word "I." Circle every answer that still begins with "I call," "I approve" or "I know where that is." Beside each circle, add who else could act, what they would need and what would stop without the owner. Now you have a first working map someone else can inspect. It does not prove the business is sellable or change its value. It shows which relationships, decisions and records still have no handoff.
linkedin.standalone_payoff: The viewer receives a working dependency-mapping exercise and its factual limit.

pilots.visual_core: Manav gives the no-I constraint; illustrative I-call, I-approve and I-know answers attach to the owner; the dependencies move into a map with actor, access and stop-condition fields; Manav returns to state the limit and platform close.

pilots.narrow_loop: Replace two spreadsheet assumptions with one delivery-time observation and one price-response observation.
pilots.larger_loop: What offer, channel test and stop conditions make the service worth testing?

youtube.spoken_copy: This model misses my target. I'm not fixing it. Eight modeled engagements at twelve thousand produce ninety-six thousand gross. After ten thousand in modeled costs, eighty-six thousand remains before owner pay and tax. It falls short of my one hundred twenty thousand dollar target. These are assumptions, not observed performance or a forecast. More clients assumes the work fits and the clients can be found. A higher fee assumes someone pays it. So I would time one engagement and make one real offer. That gives me one delivery-time observation and one price response. Neither proves the market. EP007 adds the channel test and the conditions that would stop me from building it.
youtube.standalone_payoff: Collect one delivery-time observation and one price-response observation before changing the spreadsheet.
youtube.episode_extension: The complete offer, operating boundary, channel test and stop conditions.
youtube.cta: EP007 adds the channel test and the conditions that would stop me from building it.
youtube.cliffhanger_line: What other answers would end the experiment?

linkedin.spoken_copy: A model that misses its target can still be useful. Fixing it without evidence makes it less honest. In this scenario, eight engagements leave eighty-six thousand dollars before owner pay and tax, below a one hundred twenty thousand dollar target. This is not observed performance or an earnings forecast. Adding clients assumes the work fits and the clients can be found. Raising the fee assumes someone accepts it. Time one engagement. Make one real offer. The first gives a delivery-time observation. The second gives a price response. Neither proves the market. Both tell you more than changing the cell.
linkedin.standalone_payoff: The viewer gets an operator rule for replacing model assumptions with bounded observations.

pilots.visual_core: Manav opens beside the target miss; modeled values route from eight engagements to gross and costs; more clients and higher fee appear as unsupported repairs; the spreadsheet splits into a stopwatch test and an actual-offer test; Manav lands the distinction.

pilots.narrow_loop: Distinguish agreement with the problem from a pre-deadline paid commitment.
pilots.larger_loop: What is the smallest offer, and do brokers already perform enough of the work free to remove the channel?

youtube.spoken_copy: The work can exist. The budget might not. Years before a sale, an owner may need operations written down, records cleaned and the work in their head made visible. But there may be no buyer or deadline. Near a transaction, brokers, accountants and lawyers have clear roles. That can be fair when the owner does not want to pay for a sale that may never happen. So this may be a service. Or work everyone agrees with and nobody funds. Make one paid offer. If an owner says it matters but will not pay yet, that is agreement. It is not evidence of demand. The warning is when that keeps happening. EP007 tests the other risk: brokers may already do enough of this work free.
youtube.standalone_payoff: Agreement with the problem is not demand evidence; record the response to a paid offer and look for a repeated pattern.
youtube.episode_extension: The bounded offer and whether brokers already perform enough of the work free to remove the front door.
youtube.cta: EP007 tests the other risk: brokers may already do enough of this work free.
youtube.cliffhanger_line: Do brokers already do enough of this work free?

linkedin.spoken_copy: A service gap is not proof of demand. It may be work with no budget yet. Near a business sale, brokers, accountants, lawyers and advisers have clear roles. That can be fair to an owner who does not want to pay for a sale that never happens. Years earlier, the owner may still need operations written down, records cleaned and the work in their head made visible. That gap may support a fixed-fee preparation service. It is still only a hypothesis. Make one paid offer before a buyer or deadline exists. If an owner says it matters but will not pay yet, that is agreement. It is not evidence of demand. The warning is when that keeps happening.
linkedin.standalone_payoff: The viewer receives a paid-offer observation rule and a warning to look for a repeated pattern.
